findings.pdf_says: 8.7.5.1 Format 1 (simple-relational-operator): the six alternatives 'IS GREATER THAN / IS > / IS LESS THAN / IS < / IS EQUAL TO / IS =' are enclosed in a full-height pair of BRACES — a curly '{' on the left and a curly '}' on the right (verified at 300 dpi, crop of the figure). There are no vertical choice-indicator bars inside the braces.
findings.markdown_says:
```
⌐                      ¬
| IS GREATER THAN       |
| IS >                  |
| IS LESS THAN          |
| IS <                  |
| IS EQUAL TO           |
| IS =                  |
L                      ┘
```
findings.why_it_matters: Per 5.2.6 braces enclose alternatives of which exactly one SHALL be selected, while brackets enclose material that may be omitted. The markdown draws the delimiter with square-corner glyphs (⌐ ¬ L ┘) that read as a bracket/box, not as the brace glyphs (⎧⎫⎩⎭) this transcription uses for braces elsewhere (e.g. page 215, page 217). A reader consuming the markdown cannot tell that a simple-relational-operator requires exactly one of the six forms; the bracket reading makes the whole operator optional.
findings.suggested_repair: Redraw the Format 1 figure with the brace glyphs used on pages 215/217 (⎧ ⎪ ⎨ ⎩ / ⎫ ⎪ ⎬ ⎭) and add a 'Figure notes' blockquote stating the braces are plain (exactly one alternative selected, no choice indicators). The Format 2 (extended-relational-operator) figure on page 204 has the identical defect (drawn with ┌─┐ / │ / └┘ box glyphs) and should be fixed in the same change set.

findings.pdf_says: In Format 1 the words GREATER, LESS and EQUAL are UNDERLINED; IS, THAN and TO are printed without an underline, and the relational characters '>', '<', '=' carry no underline.
findings.markdown_says:
| IS GREATER THAN       |
| IS >                  |
| IS LESS THAN          |
| IS <                  |
| IS EQUAL TO           |
| IS =                  |   (no underlining anywhere, and no 'Figure notes' paragraph for this figure)
findings.why_it_matters: Per 8.3.1.2/8.3.1.3 (and the convention stated at 5.2.x) underlined words in a general format are KEYWORDS (required) and non-underlined uppercase words are OPTIONAL words. With the underlining dropped and no Figure notes paragraph to record it, the markdown gives no way to derive that 'IS' and 'THAN'/'TO' are optional while GREATER/LESS/EQUAL are required. Every other figure in this transcription records this (225 'Figure notes' blockquotes exist; page 223 even preserves inline underlining as '[ <u>NOT</u> ] boolean-expression-1'), so this figure is an outlier.
findings.suggested_repair: Add the standard 'Figure notes (relational operator Format 1 (simple-relational-operator) syntax diagram)' blockquote after the figure: GREATER, LESS and EQUAL are underlined in the printed standard (required words); IS, THAN and TO are not underlined (optional words); the character operators >, < and = are not underlined but are required when that alternative is used (see 5.2.x on special character words); the braces are plain — exactly one alternative shall be selected; no choice indicators are present. Do the same for Format 2 on page 204 (GREATER, LESS, EQUAL, NOT, OR underlined).

findings.pdf_says: Table 4 — Combination of symbols in boolean expressions has a two-level header: the corner cell 'First Symbol' plus a spanning header cell 'Second symbol' printed above the five column headers 'Identifier or literal', 'B-AND B-OR B-XOR B-SHIFT-L B-SHIFT-R B-SHIFT-LC B-SHIFT-RC', 'B-NOT', '(' and ')'.
findings.markdown_says: | **First Symbol** | **Identifier or literal** | **B-AND B-OR B-XOR B-SHIFT-L B-SHIFT-R B-SHIFT-LC B-SHIFT-RC** | **B-NOT** | **(** | **)** |
findings.why_it_matters: The spanning label 'Second symbol' is the only thing that tells the reader the columns are the SECOND symbol of the pair while the rows are the first; without it the table's axes are unlabelled and a permissible-pair lookup can be read backwards. Table 3 on page 205 does keep its 'Second symbol' label, so the omission is inconsistent as well as lossy.
findings.suggested_repair: Restore the group header, e.g. add a preceding header line '| | Second symbol | | | | |' (or an explicit note above the table) so the column-group label is present as it is for Table 3.

findings.pdf_says: Table 3 — Combinations of symbols in arithmetic expressions: header 'First symbol' in the corner, 'Second symbol' spanning, then the five column headers 'Identifier or literal', '+ – * / **', 'Unary + or –', '(' and ')'.
findings.markdown_says:
| First symbol | Second symbol | | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| | **Identifier or literal** | **+ – * / \*\*** | **Unary + or –** | **(** | **)** |
findings.why_it_matters: The header/delimiter rows declare 5 columns but the sub-header row supplies 6 cells. Under CommonMark/GFM table rules cells beyond the declared column count are discarded, so the ')' column header disappears from the rendered table, and the continuation rows on page 206 (which are written as a separate 6-column table) no longer line up with this header.
findings.suggested_repair: Make the whole of Table 3 one 6-column table: header '| First symbol | Second symbol | | | | |' (6 cells) with a 6-column delimiter row, keep the sub-header row as the second header line, and join the page-206 body rows to the same table.

findings.pdf_says: Items 'c)', 'd)' and 'e)' are indented one level, subordinate to item '2) When the value of operand-2 is greater than zero, the results shall be determined as follows:' (begun on page 208); items '3)' and '4)' then return to the outer margin.
findings.markdown_says:
c) When operand-2 is an integer and the following condition is true
...
e) Otherwise, the equivalent arithmetic expression is defined by the implementor. ...

3) When operand-2 is less than zero, ...

4) When both operand-1 and operand-2 are equal to zero, ...   (c/d/e written flush left, at the same indentation as 3) and 4))
findings.why_it_matters: In 8.8.1.4.4 the a)–e) cases apply only when operand-2 is greater than zero, whereas 3) and 4) are independent rules. Page 208 does indent a) and b) three spaces under 2); losing the indentation for c)–e) at the page break detaches them from their parent and makes them look like peers of 3) and 4).
findings.suggested_repair: Indent the c), d), e) blocks (and their embedded expression lines) three spaces, matching the a)/b) items on page 208, so the sub-list stays attached to item 2).
